paper.title: New system responses to juvenile crime: Experiences from Denmark
paper.journal: Nordisk Tidsskrift for Kriminalvidenskab, nr. 3/2023, pp. 332-350
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement is printed. The article states that the quantitative analyses use administrative data from the Danish Police, administrative information from the Youth Crime Boards and the Youth Probation Service, …

registers.name_in_paper: administrative data from the Danish Police on registered offences committed by 10-17-year-olds (police records of violent YCB offences)
registers.role: outcome counts and the denominator for referral shares (Table 1)
variables_mentioned: violent YCB offences (all types of violent crime, robbery, extortion, sexual offences, aggravated arson)

registers.name_in_paper: administrative information from YCBs and the YPS on referrals and adjudications (annual reports from the Youth Crime Board)
registers.role: treatment-system case counts: referrals to YCBs, adjudications, cases referred to the YPS and the interventions included in improvement programmes (Tables 1, 2 and 3; Figure 3)

registers.name_in_paper: Information provided by the Danish Probation Service / the Danish Prison and Probation Service
registers.role: pre-reform comparison: juvenile probationers by age at enrolment and by programme length (Table A2, Figure 3)
verdicts for juveniles aged 15-17 prosecuted for a violent offence (Table A1), used to explain why 15-17-year-olds are underrepresented among YCB referrals
variables_mentioned: case dismissed, state of the evidence

linkages: No individual-level record linkage is described: the quantitative material consists of aggregate counts by age and year taken from separate administrative sources (police records, YCB annual reports, the Danish Probation Service and Statistics Denmark).
Qualitative interviews with 12 child welfare case managers are analysed alongside, but not linked to, the administrative counts.

sample.universe: Juveniles aged 10-17 in Denmark who committed a violent YCB offence registered by the police (2017-2021), cases referred to and adjudicated by Youth Crime Boards and supervised by the Youth Probation Service (2019-2021), and, for the pre-reform comparison, juvenile probationers aged 15-17 in the Danish Probation Service (2018-2019)
sample.unit_of_observation: Case (registered offence, referral, adjudication or probation programme), reported as aggregate counts by single year of age and calendar year; plus 12 interviewed child welfare case managers
selection_rules: Offences are restricted to the category 'violent YCB offences': all types of violent crime plus robbery, extortion, sexual offences (sexual assault, rape) and aggravated arson (Table 1 note).
Cases in the category 'serious and repeated offending' are screened by the police and could not be included in the offence counts (footnote 3, p. 6).
Offenders are aged 10-17 (10-14 suspected of, 15-17 convicted of, a qualifying offence).
Pre-reform probation figures cover juveniles aged 15-17 supervised by the Danish Probation Service in 2018 and 2019.
Qualitative material: 12 case managers in municipal child welfare services.
sample.n_observations: Table 1: 3242 (2017), 3279 (2018), 3884 (2019), 4188 (2020) and 3382 (2021) reported violent YCB offences, and 607 (2019), 909 (2020) and 1037 (2021) referrals to YCBs. Table 2: 475 (2019), 559 (2020) and 696 (2021) adjudications referred to the YPS. Table A2: 185 (2018) and 186 (2019) juvenile cases in the Danish Probation Service. Table A1: 986 convictions of 15-17-year-olds in 2021.
sample.n_individuals: 12 interviewed case managers; the administrative figures are case counts, not person counts

construction_notes: The category 'violent YCB offences' includes all types of violent crimes as well as robbery, extortion, sexual offences (sexual assault, rape), and aggravated arson (note to Table 1, p. 7).

Cases in the category 'serious and repeated offending' are subject to police screening and could not be included in the reported offence counts; they make up 3.5 percent of cases with 10-14-year-olds and 10.7 percent of cases with 15-17-year-olds (p. 6).

Pre-reform probation figures cover 15-17-year-olds in the Danish Probation Service while post-reform figures cover 10-17-year-olds in the Youth Probation Service, so the two populations differ in age coverage by construction.

Figure 3 compares programme length for the 185 Danish Probation Service cases in 2018 (93 under 12 months, 64 at 12 months, 26 at 24 months) with YPS cases in 2021 (175 under 12 months, 252 at 12 months, 129 at 13-23 months and 131 at 24 months).
No individual-level Danish register (BEF, IND, RAS, ...) is used: the article works with aggregate administrative counts and one Statistics Denmark statbank table (STRAF40).

claims.statement: After the 2019 reform the number of juveniles aged 10-17 supervised in the probation system each year rose to 696 cases in the Youth Probation Service in 2021, against 185 juvenile cases in the Danish Probation Service in 2018 -- a tripling, in the authors' words.

timing.value: Annual case counts, 2018 (pre-reform) and 2021 (post-reform)

units.value: number of juvenile probation cases in the year (2021)

magnitude.interpretation: "the number of juveniles in the probation system has tripled"

estimand.target_population: Juveniles aged 10-17 in Denmark under probation-type supervision
estimand.time_horizon: 2021, the third calendar year of the new system, against 2018, the last full year before it

Absent the reform, the number of juveniles under probation supervision would have stayed at its pre-reform level

claims.statement: The share of police-registered violent YCB offences committed by 10-17-year-olds that is referred to a Youth Crime Board rose over the first three years of the new system, from 16 percent in 2019 to almost 33 percent in 2021.

treatment.label: Calendar year of operation of the new system (2019, 2020, 2021)

definition.value: Year in which referrals to Youth Crime Boards are counted, over the first three years after the 2019 reform

outcome.label: Share of reported violent YCB offences committed by juveniles that is referred to Youth Crime Boards

definition.value: Number of new cases referred to YCBs in a year divided by the number of violent YCB offences reported to the police by 10-17-year-olds in that year (Table 1)

units.value: percent of reported violent YCB offences referred to YCBs in 2021 (the paper writes 'almost 33 percent')

magnitude.interpretation: "in 2019, the number of new cases referred to YCBs corresponds to 16 percent of the reported YCB offences committed by juveniles, in 2020 to 22 percent, and in 2021, almost 33 percent of the offences were referred to YCBs"

identification.source_of_variation: Implementation of the YCBs over their first three years of operation, 2019-2021

key_assumptions.assumption: Referrals counted in a year concern offences registered in the same year, so that the ratio can be read as a referral share
Police registration practice for violent offences by 10-17-year-olds is stable across 2019-2021
The denominator covers only violent YCB offences: cases in the category 'serious and repeated offending' are subject to police screening and could not be included in the reporting
key_assumptions.supported_by: Footnote 3 (p. 6) states the exclusion; the text reports that this category makes up 3.5 percent of cases with 10-14-year-olds and 10.7 percent of cases with 15-17-year-olds (Youth Crime Board, 2022)

implies_edges.to: Inclusion in the reported offence counts

threats_discussed: Cases with 15-17-year-olds reach the YCB only after a court verdict, which creates a time lag in processing (p. 7).
Only 50 percent of violent offences committed by 15-17-year-olds are sanctioned with a prison sentence and many cases are dropped for lack of evidence (p. 7, Table A1).
